children: Cocoa futures recovered on Tuesday after setting 7-1/2-week lows earlier in the session, while raw sugar also turned higher after slumping to a 4-week low.
COCOA
* London cocoa
rose 2.6% to £4,060 per metric ton by 1323 GMT. The market had earlier set a 7-1/2-week low of £3,799.
* Dealers said recent weakness had been driven by excess supplies although a more balanced market is expected in the 2026/27 season with global production set to fall.

* Rainfall was below average last week in most of Ivory Coast's main cocoa-growing regions, and farmers said on Monday that dry conditions could threaten the development of small pods due to be harvested next year during the September-to-February main crop.
* New York cocoa
gained 2.3% to $5,476 a ton after hitting a 7-1/2-week low of $5,111.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 0.6% to 17.58 cents per lb after setting a 4-week low of 17.11 cents.

* Dealers said the market's pullback from a 16-month high of 18.88 cents set on September 10 still may have further to go although the outlook is more constructive in the medium to long-term with an El Nino weather event set to dent production and potentially lead to a global deficit in the 2026/27 season.

* Indonesia is expected to experience a shorter than usual rainy season starting November this year, the weather agency said on Tuesday, which could impact crops as farmers adjust their planting schedules.
* Indonesia's sugarcane harvest next year is expected to come late as farmers typically wait for the beginning of the rainy season to start planting.
* White sugar
fell 0.1% to $507 a ton after setting a 6-1/2-week low of $496.80.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
fell 0.2% to $2.7585 per lb after hitting a 3-month low of $2.7260.
* Dealers said generally favourable crop weather in top producers Brazil and Vietnam had contributed to recent weakness.
* Robusta coffee
lost 1.35% to $3,292 a ton.
